title: Box-Cox transformation for a list of numbers (forward: original scale to transformed scale)
label2: Type in one or more positive numeric values (comma-separated) to be transformed using the Box-Cox transformation with the specified Lambda (λ)
inputNumbers: Type in one or more positive numeric values separated by commas (e.g. 47.5, 50.2, 53.6)
useStoredRad: Option 1: Use the Lambda (λ) stored with a variable from the dataset (bcox_lambda attribute from a prior Box-Cox transformation)
variableSelcted: Select a variable with a stored Box-Cox Lambda (λ)
manualLambdaRad: Option 2: Manually specify the Lambda (λ) value (in the range -2 to 2)
digits: Digits - rounds to the specified number of decimal places

help.title: Box-Cox transformation for a list of numbers
help.body:
Description
Apply the Box-Cox transformation (forward direction: original scale to transformed scale) to one or more user-supplied positive numeric values. The Lambda (λ) is obtained from either a variable with a stored bcox_lambda attribute or manually entered

This is useful for transforming specification limits, targets, or any reference values using the same Box-Cox Lambda that was fitted to a dataset - for example, before running a capability analysis on the transformed scale, or to check what a particular original-scale value maps to in the transformed space

All input values must be strictly positive (X > 0) - the Box-Cox transformation is not defined for zero or negative values

Box-Cox transformation
λ = 0 : Y = Ln( X )
λ ≠ 0 : Y = ( X^λ - 1 ) / λ

Lambda (λ) values associated with familiar transformations
λ = 2: square transformation ( x^2 )
λ = 1: no transformation; returns the original data ( x )
λ = 0.50: square root transformation ( sqrt(x) )
λ = 0.33: cube root transformation
λ = 0.25: fourth root transformation
λ = 0: natural log transformation ( log(x) )
λ = -0.50: reciprocal square root transformation ( 1/sqrt(x) )
λ = -1: reciprocal (inverse) transformation ( 1/x )
λ = -2: reciprocal square transformation ( 1/x^2 )

For the detail help on Box-Cox or Lambda (λ) - use R help(boxcox, package = MASS)

For a good overview of MASS Box-Cox, see https://www.css.cornell.edu/faculty/dgr2/_static/files/R_html/Transformations.html
